claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model should be certified for launch now based on aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, despite a 1.3 percentage-point miss in the utility arrears assistance segment and an unresolved disclosure question.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness but are not sufficient if a separate mandatory disclosure predicate is unmet.
A weakness affecting a named launch use case is material under the governing policy text.
For a material limitation, certification before launch requires one of: resolution of the issue, required disclosure, or approved risk acceptance.
Public governance principles may inform good practice, but they do not override the stated internal release policy.
evidence_requests: Produce admissible evidence that the utility arrears assistance limitation was disclosed in the model card or other required launch disclosure.
Produce an approved risk-acceptance record covering this exact named launch use case before launch.
Produce a final legal determination closing the disclosure question.
Produce admissible evidence that the segment is not in fact a named launch use case or contractual/customer commitment, if that is being contested.
specific_concerns: The affected segment is a named launch use case in two rollout commitments, which makes the weakness material under the policy text.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
There is admissible evidence of an open legal ticket on whether disclosure is required, and no admissible evidence of a final legal determination, actual disclosure, or approved risk acceptance.
The Actor's packet relies on aggregate readiness and public governance principles, but those do not satisfy the specific internal policy predicate for launch certification in this case.
The 'non-core' or 7% traffic framing does not resolve materiality where the segment is named in customer commitments and legal review is pending.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant now, absent evidence that the material limitation has been disclosed, resolved, or accepted through an approved risk-acceptance process.
That public risk-management and model-card guidance can substitute for satisfaction of the internal release-policy requirement.
Any implicit claim that the named-segment issue is immaterial because it affects only 7% of projected first-month traffic.
